description: Organize cloud storage: audit the current structure, define the folder hierarchy and naming convention, reorganize files, set permissions, configure retention rules, and produce the storage organization plan.

steps.description: Audit the current cloud storage structure, file naming patterns, and usage across folders.

inputs.name: storage-platform
inputs.desc: The cloud storage platform in use (Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, S3, or multiple)

inputs.name: team-size
inputs.desc: Number of people using the storage and their roles

outputs.name: folder-inventory
outputs.desc: Current folder tree with file counts, sizes, and last-modified dates

outputs.name: naming-issues
outputs.desc: List of naming inconsistencies, duplicates, and orphaned files

process: Walk the top-level folder tree and record the depth, file count, and total size of each branch.
Flag naming inconsistencies: mixed casing, date formats, abbreviations, and special characters.
Identify duplicate files by name and size, orphaned files with no clear owner, and folders with no recent activity.
Summarize the findings into a folder inventory and a naming issues list.

steps.description: Define the target folder hierarchy, naming convention, and organizational rules.

inputs.name: folder-inventory
inputs.desc: Current folder tree from the audit

inputs.name: naming-issues
inputs.desc: Naming problems identified in the audit

outputs.name: folder-hierarchy
outputs.desc: Target folder tree with descriptions of what goes where

outputs.name: naming-convention
outputs.desc: Naming rules for files and folders (format, date handling, versioning)

process: Group the existing folders by function (projects, departments, shared resources, archive).
Design the target hierarchy with no more than four levels of nesting.
Define the naming convention: lowercase or title case, date format, version suffix, separator character.
Document where each category of file belongs in the new structure.

steps.description: Move and rename existing files to match the new hierarchy and naming convention.

outputs.name: migration-log
outputs.desc: Record of every file moved or renamed, with old and new paths

outputs.name: exceptions-list
outputs.desc: Files that could not be moved automatically and require manual review

process: Create the target folder structure in the storage platform.
Move files in batches, starting with the largest and most active folders.
Rename files that violate the naming convention, logging the old and new names.
Flag files that cannot be moved (permission issues, active links, ambiguous ownership) for manual review.

steps.description: Set up access permissions by folder based on team roles and sharing requirements.

outputs.name: permissions-matrix
outputs.desc: Who can read, write, and share each folder

outputs.name: sharing-rules
outputs.desc: Rules for external sharing, link expiration, and download permissions

process: Map each folder to the roles that need access (owner, editor, viewer).
Configure the permissions in the storage platform, removing inherited permissions where they conflict.
Set the external sharing rules: which folders allow external links, expiration defaults, and download restrictions.
Document the permissions matrix for onboarding and audits.

steps.description: Configure the retention and archival rules for files based on type and age.

outputs.name: retention-schedule
outputs.desc: How long each category of file is kept active, archived, and deleted

outputs.name: storage-organization-plan
outputs.desc: Complete plan covering hierarchy, naming, permissions, and retention

process: Classify folders by retention need: active (current projects), reference (long-term), archive (historical), and disposable (temporary).
Set the retention period for each category (e.g., active = indefinite, archive = 3 years, disposable = 90 days).
Configure automated archival or deletion rules where the platform supports them.
Compile the full storage organization plan: hierarchy, naming convention, permissions, and retention schedule.

description: Set up a file format conversion pipeline: define input and output formats, select tools, configure batch processing, handle quality checks, and produce the pipeline document.

steps.description: Define the input and output formats, volume, and quality requirements for the conversion pipeline.

inputs.name: source-formats
inputs.desc: List of input file formats (e.g., PDF, DOCX, PNG, MP4, WAV)

inputs.name: target-formats
inputs.desc: Desired output formats for each input type

outputs.name: conversion-matrix
outputs.desc: Source-to-target format mapping with quality and size requirements

outputs.name: volume-estimate
outputs.desc: Expected file count and total size per conversion type

process: List every source-to-target format pair needed.
For each pair, note the quality requirements (resolution, bitrate, compression level, OCR accuracy).
Estimate the volume: how many files per day, week, or batch, and the average file size.
Identify any special handling: password-protected files, multi-page documents, or embedded media.

steps.description: Select the conversion tools and libraries for each format pair.

outputs.name: tool-selection
outputs.desc: Selected tool or library for each conversion pair with rationale

outputs.name: infrastructure-plan
outputs.desc: Where the tools run (local, server, cloud function) and resource needs

process: For each format pair, identify the candidate tools (FFmpeg, ImageMagick, LibreOffice, Pandoc, Tesseract, custom scripts).
Evaluate each tool on quality, speed, cost, and ease of automation.
Select one tool per pair and note any configuration (codec, quality preset, DPI).
Plan the infrastructure: local machine for low volume, server or cloud function for high volume.

steps.description: Configure the batch processing workflow: input folder, triggers, processing steps, and output folder.

inputs.name: tool-selection
inputs.desc: Selected tools for each conversion pair

outputs.name: batch-config
outputs.desc: Configuration for the batch processing workflow (folders, triggers, steps, error handling)

outputs.name: conversion-pipeline-doc
outputs.desc: Complete pipeline documentation covering formats, tools, workflow, and quality checks

process: Define the input folder (or upload endpoint) and the output folder for each conversion type.
Configure the trigger: watch folder for new files, scheduled batch, or manual trigger.
Chain the processing steps: validate input, convert, verify output quality, move to output folder.
Set up error handling: retry on failure, quarantine bad files, notify on repeated errors.
Compile the pipeline documentation.

description: Set up automated file backups: inventory data sources, define the schedule and retention, configure the destination, automate the process, test restore, and produce the backup setup document.

steps.description: Inventory all data sources that need to be backed up.

inputs.name: system-inventory
inputs.desc: List of systems, servers, and devices that hold data

inputs.name: data-criticality
inputs.desc: How critical each data source is (mission-critical, important, nice-to-have)

outputs.name: backup-scope
outputs.desc: List of data sources to back up with size, change rate, and criticality

outputs.name: exclusion-list
outputs.desc: Data explicitly excluded from backup with rationale

process: List every data source: databases, file servers, cloud storage, SaaS applications, local machines.
For each source, record the data size, daily change rate, and criticality level.
Identify data that does not need backup: temporary files, build artifacts, publicly available data.
Produce the backup scope and exclusion list.

steps.description: Define the backup schedule, retention policy, and recovery objectives.

inputs.name: backup-scope
inputs.desc: Data sources to back up with criticality

outputs.name: backup-schedule
outputs.desc: Frequency for each data source (continuous, daily, weekly, monthly)

outputs.name: retention-policy
outputs.desc: How long each backup is kept and the recovery point and time objectives (RPO, RTO)

process: Set the recovery point objective (RPO) for each criticality level: how much data loss is acceptable.
Set the recovery time objective (RTO): how quickly each source must be restored.
Design the schedule to meet the RPO: continuous replication, daily incremental, weekly full.
Define the retention: how many daily, weekly, and monthly backups to keep.

steps.description: Configure the backup destinations: local, cloud, and offsite.

outputs.name: destination-config
outputs.desc: Backup destinations for each source with storage tier and encryption settings

outputs.name: cost-estimate
outputs.desc: Monthly and annual storage cost by destination

process: Select the primary destination for each source: local NAS, cloud object storage, or managed backup service.
Configure a secondary destination for critical data (3-2-1 rule: 3 copies, 2 media types, 1 offsite).
Set the storage tier (hot, cool, archive) based on access frequency and retention period.
Enable encryption at rest and in transit for all destinations.

steps.description: Set up the backup automation and test the restore process.

outputs.name: automation-config
outputs.desc: Backup jobs configured in the backup tool with schedule and notification settings

outputs.name: restore-test-result
outputs.desc: Results of restoring a sample backup to verify data integrity

process: Configure the backup jobs in the selected tool (rsync, rclone, Veeam, AWS Backup, or platform-native).
Set up notifications for backup success, failure, and storage threshold alerts.
Run the first backup for each source and verify it completed without errors.
Perform a test restore of a sample dataset and verify the restored data matches the original.

steps.description: Compile the backup setup document covering scope, schedule, destinations, automation, and restore procedures.

outputs.name: backup-setup-document
outputs.desc: Complete backup plan with scope, schedule, destinations, automation, and restore procedures

outputs.name: runbook
outputs.desc: Step-by-step restore runbook for each data source

process: Compile the backup plan: scope, schedule, retention, destinations, encryption, and costs.
Write the restore runbook: step-by-step instructions for restoring each data source from each destination.
Include the test restore results as validation that the process works.
Set the review cadence: quarterly backup audit and annual restore drill.

description: Set up a media asset management system: inventory assets, define metadata, upload and tag, configure search and access, and produce the asset management setup document.

steps.description: Inventory all media assets across storage locations.

inputs.name: storage-locations
inputs.desc: Where media files currently live (local drives, cloud storage, external drives, SaaS platforms)

inputs.name: asset-types
inputs.desc: Types of media to manage (images, videos, audio, PDFs, presentations)

outputs.name: asset-catalog
outputs.desc: List of all media files with type, size, location, and creation date

outputs.name: duplicate-report
outputs.desc: Files that appear in multiple locations or under different names

process: Scan each storage location for files matching the specified media types.
Record each file's name, type, size, creation date, and current location.
Identify duplicates by file hash or name-plus-size matching.
Produce the asset catalog and duplicate report.

steps.description: Define the metadata schema for tagging and organizing media assets.

outputs.name: metadata-schema
outputs.desc: Fields, categories, and controlled vocabularies for tagging assets

outputs.name: tagging-guidelines
outputs.desc: Rules for how to tag each asset type consistently

process: Define the required fields: title, description, category, tags, creation date, creator, usage rights, expiration.
Create the controlled vocabulary for categories and tags (no free-text where a picklist works).
Set the tagging rules: minimum number of tags, naming format, how to handle rights and expiration.
Document the schema and guidelines.

steps.description: Upload and tag existing assets according to the metadata schema.

outputs.name: tagged-asset-count
outputs.desc: Number of assets uploaded and tagged

outputs.name: tagging-exceptions
outputs.desc: Assets that could not be tagged automatically and need manual review

process: Deduplicate the asset catalog, keeping the highest-quality version of each file.
Batch-upload the deduplicated files to the asset management platform.
Auto-tag where possible (extract EXIF data, file name patterns, folder context).
Flag assets that lack enough information for manual tagging.

steps.description: Configure the search interface, access permissions, and download tracking.

inputs.name: tagged-asset-count
inputs.desc: Number of uploaded and tagged assets

outputs.name: access-config
outputs.desc: Who can search, view, download, and edit assets

outputs.name: asset-management-document
outputs.desc: Complete setup document for the media asset management system

process: Configure the search: full-text search on metadata fields, filter by category, type, date, and rights status.
Set access permissions by role: viewers can browse and download, editors can upload and tag, admins can delete and manage schema.
Enable download tracking so you know which assets are used and by whom.
Compile the asset management setup document.

description: Build a document template library: inventory recurring documents, create templates, organize by category, set up versioning, and produce the template library document.

steps.description: Inventory the recurring document types that need templates.

inputs.name: department-list
inputs.desc: Departments or teams that produce recurring documents

outputs.name: template-inventory
outputs.desc: List of recurring document types with frequency, audience, and current state

outputs.name: priority-list
outputs.desc: Templates ranked by frequency of use and impact of inconsistency

process: Interview each department to identify their recurring documents (proposals, reports, invoices, letters, presentations, SOWs).
For each document type, record how often it is created, who the audience is, and whether a template exists today.
Rank the templates by frequency and the cost of inconsistency (client-facing first, internal second).
Produce the template inventory and priority list.

steps.description: Create the standard templates with branding, placeholder fields, and instructions.

outputs.name: template-files
outputs.desc: The actual template files (DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, or platform-native)

outputs.name: usage-instructions
outputs.desc: Instructions for filling out each template correctly

process: For each template, set the page layout, header/footer, and branding elements (logo, colors, fonts).
Add placeholder fields with clear labels (e.g., [Client Name], [Project Start Date], [Deliverable Description]).
Write brief inline instructions where the user needs guidance (e.g., 'Summarize the scope in 2-3 sentences').
Save each template in the appropriate format.

steps.description: Organize the templates into a library with categories, versioning, and an approval process.

outputs.name: library-structure
outputs.desc: The organized template library with categories, naming, and version numbers

outputs.name: template-library-document
outputs.desc: Complete guide to the template library: what is available, how to find it, and how to request changes

process: Organize templates into categories (sales, operations, finance, HR, legal, marketing).
Set the naming convention: [Category]-[Document Type]-v[Version] (e.g., Sales-Proposal-v1.0).
Define the versioning and approval process: who can edit a template, how changes are reviewed, and how new versions are published.
Compile the template library document with a table of contents, usage instructions, and the change request process.

description: Set up a secure file sharing workflow: define requirements, select methods, configure access controls, set up audit logging, and produce the file sharing setup document.

steps.description: Define the file sharing requirements: who shares what with whom, and the security constraints.

inputs.name: sharing-scenarios
inputs.desc: Common file sharing scenarios (internal team, external client, one-time delivery, ongoing collaboration)

inputs.name: security-requirements
inputs.desc: Data sensitivity levels and compliance requirements (encryption, retention, access logging)

outputs.name: sharing-matrix
outputs.desc: Who shares what type of files with whom, via what method, with what controls

outputs.name: compliance-constraints
outputs.desc: Regulatory or policy requirements that affect how files can be shared

process: List the common sharing scenarios: internal team collaboration, external client delivery, vendor exchange, public distribution.
For each scenario, identify the file types, sensitivity level, and recipient type.
Map the compliance constraints: encryption requirements, geographic restrictions, retention rules, audit obligations.
Produce the sharing matrix and compliance constraints.

steps.description: Select the sharing method for each scenario and configure the access controls.

outputs.name: method-selection
outputs.desc: Selected sharing method for each scenario (link, portal, SFTP, email, API)

outputs.name: access-controls
outputs.desc: Access settings for each method (password, expiration, download limit, IP restriction)

process: For each scenario, select the sharing method: cloud link for casual internal sharing, secure portal for client delivery, SFTP for automated exchange, encrypted email for sensitive one-offs.
Configure the access controls: password protection, link expiration, download limits, and viewer-only restrictions.
Handle large file transfers: set the size threshold and the method for files that exceed email limits.
Document the method selection and access controls.

steps.description: Set up audit logging and compile the file sharing setup document.

outputs.name: audit-config
outputs.desc: Audit logging setup: what is logged, where, and who reviews the logs

outputs.name: file-sharing-setup-document
outputs.desc: Complete file sharing workflow document covering methods, controls, and audit procedures

process: Enable audit logging on each sharing platform: who shared what, with whom, when, and whether it was accessed.
Set up alerts for anomalous sharing (large volumes, sensitive files, unexpected recipients).
Define the log review cadence: weekly for high-sensitivity, monthly for standard.
Compile the file sharing setup document.

description: Set up a digital archive for long-term preservation: define scope, select format and media, migrate files, create the catalog, set access procedures, and produce the archive setup document.

steps.description: Define what to archive, the preservation standards, and the access requirements.

inputs.name: content-sources
inputs.desc: Sources of content to archive (databases, file shares, email, websites, physical media)

inputs.name: preservation-goals
inputs.desc: Why the archive exists (legal, historical, regulatory, institutional memory)

outputs.name: archival-scope
outputs.desc: What is included and excluded from the archive with rationale

outputs.name: preservation-standard
outputs.desc: File formats, metadata requirements, and integrity checks for long-term preservation

process: Identify the content that must be preserved: contracts, financial records, project deliverables, correspondence, media.
Define the preservation standard: use open formats (PDF/A, TIFF, CSV, UTF-8 text) to avoid format obsolescence.
Set the metadata requirements: title, date, creator, description, retention period, and provenance.
Specify the integrity checks: checksums (SHA-256) for every archived file, periodic fixity checks.

steps.description: Migrate files to archival format and storage.

outputs.name: migration-log
outputs.desc: Record of every file migrated with source path, target path, format conversion, and checksum

outputs.name: migration-exceptions
outputs.desc: Files that could not be migrated and require manual handling

process: Convert files to the archival format where needed (e.g., DOCX to PDF/A, JPEG to TIFF).
Apply the metadata to each file according to the schema.
Compute the SHA-256 checksum for each archived file.
Transfer the files to the archival storage and verify the checksums match.

steps.description: Create the catalog and finding aid for the archive.

outputs.name: archive-catalog
outputs.desc: Searchable catalog of all archived items with metadata

outputs.name: finding-aid
outputs.desc: Human-readable guide to what the archive contains and how to navigate it

process: Build the catalog from the migration log: one entry per file with all metadata fields populated.
Organize the catalog by collection, date range, and content type.
Write the finding aid: an overview of the archive's scope, how it is organized, and how to search it.
Make the catalog searchable (spreadsheet, database, or static site).

steps.description: Set the access and retrieval procedures and compile the archive setup document.

outputs.name: access-procedures
outputs.desc: Who can access the archive, how to request items, and the retrieval SLA

outputs.name: archive-setup-document
outputs.desc: Complete archive setup document covering scope, standards, catalog, and access

process: Define the access roles: public, internal, restricted, and the request process for each.
Set the retrieval SLA: how quickly requested items are delivered.
Schedule the periodic fixity checks (quarterly or annually) to verify file integrity.
Compile the archive setup document.

description: Set up batch image processing: define the steps, configure input and output, automate the pipeline, handle quality review, and produce the batch processing setup document.

steps.description: Define the batch processing steps and quality requirements.

inputs.name: use-case
inputs.desc: What the processed images are used for (web publishing, print, social media, product catalog, thumbnails)

inputs.name: source-format
inputs.desc: Input image format and typical dimensions

outputs.name: processing-steps
outputs.desc: Ordered list of operations (resize, crop, watermark, compress, convert) with parameters

outputs.name: quality-criteria
outputs.desc: Acceptable output quality (minimum resolution, maximum file size, visual check criteria)

process: Define each processing step in order: resize to target dimensions, crop to aspect ratio, apply watermark, compress, convert format.
Set the parameters for each step (e.g., resize to 1200x800, compress to 85% quality, output as WebP).
Define the quality criteria: minimum resolution, maximum file size, no visible artifacts, watermark positioned correctly.
Document the processing steps and quality criteria.

steps.description: Configure the input and output folders and the processing automation.

outputs.name: pipeline-config
outputs.desc: Configuration for the batch pipeline (folders, trigger, tool commands, error handling)

outputs.name: sample-output
outputs.desc: A test batch of processed images for quality review

process: Set up the input folder (watched directory, upload endpoint, or scheduled scan).
Configure the processing tool (ImageMagick, Sharp, Pillow, or cloud service) with the step parameters.
Set up the output folder with the naming convention for processed files.
Run a test batch of 5-10 images and save the output for quality review.

steps.description: Review the sample output, adjust parameters, and finalize the pipeline setup.

outputs.name: final-config
outputs.desc: Finalized pipeline configuration after quality review adjustments

outputs.name: batch-processing-document
outputs.desc: Complete setup document for the batch image processing pipeline

process: Review each sample image against the quality criteria: resolution, file size, visual artifacts, watermark placement.
Adjust parameters where the output does not meet the criteria (reduce compression, change crop coordinates, resize watermark).
Run a second test batch to verify the adjustments.
Compile the batch processing setup document: steps, parameters, folders, triggers, error handling, and quality review schedule.
